brief: JPMorgan's Nov 20 International Market Intelligence briefing: a short-lived tech relief rally reversed into an 'everything selloff' sparing almost no sector except India, with VIX spiking to March levels. AI and Tech sit at the epicentre, pressured by China export-control concerns, cyber/data-leak worries, and capex-peaking signals from Tencent (2027 peak capex) and Alibaba (positive cash flow by 2H28). Korea and Taiwan are APAC's worst hit; Taiwan has further to fall as retail de-leveraging continues and foreign ownership stays high versus Korea, which de-risked earlier. The selloff is broadening beyond Tech as Iran-strike risk grows and Fed speak turns more hawkish, while dispersion normalizes, JPM's tracker breaking below 20% from a Q3 reading above 40%. Separately, JPM is tactically bullish on global equities: extreme Semis positioning (HF net exposure down 67% from its high, six straight weeks of selling) and depressed sentiment set up a technical, not fundamental, bounce, though 80th-percentile long-term Semis exposure argues any rebound stays shallow. US Econ flags capex and the wealth effect both moderating next year. In EMEA Mining, JPM stays selective, preferring copper names (Antofagasta, Glencore, Atalaya, ArcelorMittal, Overweight) over iron-ore peers, while cautious on Lundin Mining (Underweight) and Norsk Hydro (Neutral, negative watch).
